item.title: MCC Misuse and Misclassification — Separate Financial Evidence Track
item.lead: Merchant Category Codes (MCCs) determine how a payment is categorized by card networks and banks; an incorrect or misleading code can bypass risk monitoring and blocks.

blocks.text: Finding: MCCs are categories defined by card networks that co-determine a transaction's risk profile, permitted processing, and monitoring. Services for paid digital intimacy typically fall under high-risk categories with stricter registration and monitoring requirements.

Hypothesis: Payments can be classified via intermediaries, resellers, or generic codes (e.g., digital goods, software, or subscriptions) in such a way that the true nature of the service is less visible to the issuing bank or cardholder. This dossier does not establish that a specific platform or agency engages in this practice.

rows: Discrepancy between MCC on statement and actual service
Card statements, acquirer data, merchant descriptor
Payment via intermediate reseller or PSP
Contracts between platform, PSP, and acquirer
Time series of transactions and descriptors

blocks.label: METHODOLOGICAL DISTINCTION
blocks.text: A divergent MCC is not proof of money laundering or fraud. Only when primary documentation (statements, acquirer contracts, descriptor history) demonstrates systematic misclassification can misuse be spoken of.
